description: This solution classifies mouse social behavior from pose using hand-crafted features extracted from the context window for each frame, followed by a gradient boosting classifier. The features include within-frame and across-window statistics of inter-animal distances, within-animal body part distances (e.g., nose-to-neck), displacement and velocity features based on position differences across time offsets, and relative orientation angles between keypoints. The model employs scikit-learn's HistGradientBoostingClassifier for efficient training and robust generalization, and the code sets numpy RNG and model seeds to ensure determinism. Cross-validation is done via five-fold stratified split on the training set to select the best model configuration (using macro-F1 score); however, due to constraints, hyperparameter tuning is light and deterministic. The entire pipeline keeps memory usage and runtime suitable for a single CPU. Output is the integer label per test sample, matching the input shape.
